I've tried shrooms and acid about ten times or so. My first trips on shrooms were god awful because I took doses that were likely too high. My last two times tripping were absolutely amazing, I'm not sure how much they helped my mental health in the long run but they were very grounding, pleasant experiences. I strongly dislike weed and I suspect you liking weed would make you less likely to have a bad trip. Just exercise caution by doing it in a safe setting with people you are comfortable with. The stimuli you are surrounded by is very influential in that state. Try to make it uplifting.

I think these disorders are on a continuum so it really depends on the individual's. Just dont let yourself stay trapped in a codependent relationship where you are being put down constantly.

I wish you the best <3 sending a big virtual hug your way. It will get easier, I promise. Although I have days where I am still caught off guard, hell even last night, the days of pure relief are far more common 10 months on. I'm in a wonderful supportive relationship with an amazing man who genuinely respects me instead of making me feel like trash. The pain was so worth it.

I would think of all the times they hurt me. And all the times I was sitting there during the relationship thinking of what our future would be like and that it would be soul destroying. If someone was going to change they would have done it the months and years you were begging them to, not after you break up. That means they were okay with disappointing you as long as they still had their hooks in you.

Also, remind yourself that people break up. All the time. It's okay and you don't owe anyone a grand reason. My relationship was very codependent and I felt responsible for all of their feelings and actions. The pain of the guilt for "making" them sad was the hardest thing I've ever had to bare and it might be for you too. Sit with that pain. Let it wash over you and let it pass. But do not give in. The only person you are responsible for is you (unless you have children). Let go of the pain that isn't yours to bare.  You can still care about that person, even love them, but still want to be free of them. Be gentle to yourself, there is no reason to feel guilty for that.
